documents: Passport plus Cuban residence status or Central Bank authorisation; in practice local residency documents are needed.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Banco Metropolitano, Banco Popular de Ahorro and Banco de Credito y Comercio (USD accounts mainly for Cubans abroad, not foreign non-residents).
restrictions: US embargo and OFAC sanctions, de-risking by foreign correspondents, dual-currency and FX shortages; Resolution 73/2020 USD accounts target Cuban nationals abroad.
alternatives: Visitors rely on cash (EUR/CAD) and prepaid tourist cards; remittance channels via authorised agents; Australian-issued non-US cards may work at some ATMs.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts (Cuban banks' USD accounts target Cubans abroad), so no applicable costs.

documents: Passport (notarised copy), proof of foreign address, bank reference letter, source-of-funds evidence, TIN for CRS.
min_deposit_fees: Not published for personal accounts; BOSVG lists a nominal opening deposit (about XCD 10) on its account checklist.
banks: Bank of St. Vincent and the Grenadines (accepts notarised forms by email/fax); Republic Bank (EC) via RepublicOnboard is aimed at nationals abroad.
restrictions: Enhanced due diligence for non-residents, CRS reporting, correspondent-bank de-risking in the Eastern Caribbean; XCD pegged to USD.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for multi-currency needs; offshore-oriented international banks licensed in SVG serve non-residents but are not retail banks.
cost_note: Bank of St. Vincent and the Grenadines checklist cites a nominal opening deposit of about XCD 10 (about USD 3.70 at XCD 2.70/USD); opening and monthly fees for non-resident personal accounts are not published.

documents: Passport with entry stamp, second photo ID, proof of foreign address, bank reference letters, income statement, sometimes two local references.
min_deposit_fees: Low minimums reported, e.g. about USD 50-100 or NIO 1,000 for savings; fees not published.
banks: BAC Credomatic, Banpro, LAFISE (case-by-case for non-residents, branch visit required).
restrictions: US and EU sanctions on officials and state entities, 2024 laws widening state access to financial data, heavy KYC; USD accounts common.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut abroad; remittance services such as Xoom deliver to local accounts.
cost_note: Reported minimum opening deposits at BAC/Banpro/LAFISE are about USD 50-100 (lower bound used) or NIO 1,000 (about USD 27 at NIO 36.6/USD); opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport, proof of address, proof of income or employment, foreign bank reference letter, sometimes residence permit and tax ID.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; non-residents may face higher opening capital or minimum balances for USD/EUR accounts.
banks: De Surinaamsche Bank, Hakrinbank, Republic Bank Suriname (branch visit; no confirmed remote non-resident onboarding).
restrictions: FX shortages and post-2020 currency crisis, slow onboarding (reports of up to months), correspondent banking limits.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut held abroad; Mercury/US fintech for business needs.
cost_note: No published non-resident figures for DSB, Hakrinbank or Republic Bank Suriname; opening capital and minimum balances for USD/EUR accounts are set case by case.

documents: Passport with valid visa or visa-free entry stamp, Chinese mobile number, local address, stated purpose of account; many branches still ask for residence permit or temporary residence registration.
min_deposit_fees: Typically no or very low minimum (around CNY 10 card fee); some guides cite USD 500 for a USD account at Bank of China.
banks: Bank of China, ICBC, Bank of Beijing and other large banks (branch-dependent acceptance of short-term visitors).
restrictions: Strict capital controls (USD 50,000 annual FX quota), branch discretion, no remote opening for non-residents; tourist-visa applicants often refused.
alternatives: Alipay and WeChat Pay linked to foreign cards (PBOC 2024 easing); Wise, Revolut abroad.
cost_note: Large banks such as Bank of China and ICBC typically require no minimum for a CNY debit account and charge about CNY 10 for the card (about USD 1.40 at CNY 7.1/USD); some guides cite USD 500 for a USD account, and monthly fees for visitors are not published.

documents: Passport, second ID (often ACR I-Card), proof of local address, Philippine mobile number, sometimes reference or proof of income.
min_deposit_fees: BDO about PHP 5,000 and BPI about PHP 3,000 for peso savings; USD accounts often require higher deposits; fees not published for non-residents.
banks: BDO, BPI, Metrobank (case-by-case; non-residents mostly limited to USD/EUR foreign-currency deposit accounts).
restrictions: BSP KYC rules, ACR I-Card requirement effectively excludes short-term visitors, peso accounts often unavailable to non-residents.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for PHP; local e-wallets GCash and Maya need local ID/number.
cost_note: BPI peso savings minimum is about PHP 3,000 (about USD 52 at PHP 58/USD; BDO about PHP 5,000 = USD 86); opening and monthly fees for non-residents are not published.

documents: Passport, PNG work permit or visa, local address and employer reference; non-resident accounts require compliance with BPNG FE Manual Notice 11.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; BSP foreign-currency accounts carry minimum balances and need BPNG approval.
banks: BSP, Kina Bank, ANZ and Westpac PNG operations (non-resident personal accounts not generally offered).
restrictions: Foreign exchange controls, BPNG approval for FCAs, tax clearance needed for transfers abroad, FX shortages.
alternatives: Keep funds in Australia (ANZ/Westpac) or use Wise; local mobile money such as MiBank/CellMoni needs PNG presence.
cost_note: Non-resident personal accounts are not generally offered (BSP foreign-currency accounts need BPNG approval), so no applicable costs.

documents: Passport, proof of address, likely local address or reference and reason for account; requirements not published.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Bank of the FSM (only locally incorporated commercial bank); Bank of Guam branches (requirements not published).
restrictions: USD economy; small market with limited correspondent banking; FATCA/US banking rules apply via US-linked banks.
alternatives: Use US or Australian accounts and Wise; Bank of Guam and US online banks if eligible.
cost_note: Bank of the FSM and Bank of Guam do not publish non-resident opening fees, deposits or monthly charges.

documents: Passport (notarised translation sometimes), client questionnaire, signature card, source-of-funds explanation; local phone helpful.
min_deposit_fees: Low or no minimum deposit at most banks; card fees modest; exact non-resident fees not published.
banks: Bakai Bank, Optima Bank, Demir Bank, Kicb (non-residents accepted with branch visit or notarised power of attorney).
restrictions: Heightened scrutiny and EU/US secondary-sanctions concerns over Russia-linked flows; some banks restrict USD transfers.
alternatives: Remote opening via notarised power of attorney through intermediaries; Wise; local e-wallets (MBank) need visit.
cost_note: Bakai Bank's individual accounts page states account opening has no service fee and no monthly fee (only transactions are charged); its minimum deposit is not published (KICB reportedly charges KGS 100, about USD 1.15 at KGS 87.4/USD, to open).

documents: Passport, proof of address, tax number (NIF) and likely residence permit or local justification; requirements not published.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Banco Internacional de Sao Tome e Principe (BISTP), majority-owned by CGD; acceptance of non-residents unconfirmed.
restrictions: Central bank controls on foreign-exchange operations, slow correspondent transfers, STN pegged to EUR.
alternatives: Portuguese banks (CGD, BPI) with non-resident accounts; Wise or Revolut.
cost_note: BISTP does not publish fees or minimum deposits, and acceptance of non-residents is unconfirmed.

documents: Passport, residence or work permit, local address, KYC forms; FCDA requires a Kwacha operating account.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: National Bank of Malawi, Standard Bank Malawi (FCDA eligibility limited to exporters, NGOs, Malawians abroad).
restrictions: Exchange controls, 2024 regulations on FCDAs and mandatory conversion, chronic FX shortages.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut abroad; mobile money (Airtel Money, TNM Mpamba) needs local SIM and ID.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts (FCDA eligibility limited to exporters, NGOs and Malawians abroad), so no applicable costs.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, foreign TIN, reason or tie to the Netherlands; BSN and Dutch address usually required within 90 days at retail banks.
min_deposit_fees: No minimum deposit; ABN AMRO charges a monthly non-resident surcharge on top of standard account fees (higher tier for Australia).
banks: ABN AMRO (non-residents with a Dutch link, surcharge applies); ING and bunq require EEA residence or Dutch address.
restrictions: Strict AML/KYC, de-risking of non-EEA residents (ABN AMRO closed ~15,000 non-EEA accounts), CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut or bunq for EUR IBAN; N26 or other EU neobanks if EEA-resident.
cost_note: ABN AMRO charges no opening fee or minimum deposit, but its January 2026 non-resident surcharge puts Australia in category 2 at EUR 8.00 per account per month (about USD 9.40 at USD 1.17/EUR), on top of the regular payment-package fee which is not included here.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, source-of-funds documentation, tax ID for CRS.
min_deposit_fees: Reported EUR 500-2,000 opening deposit depending on bank; fees not published.
banks: Banca di San Marino, Cassa di Risparmio della Repubblica di San Marino, Banca Agricola Commerciale (private-banking style, case-by-case).
restrictions: CRS participant, enhanced AML after past grey-listing, account restrictions may apply initially for new non-resident clients.
alternatives: Italian or other EU banks; Wise, Revolut.
cost_note: Reported opening deposits are EUR 500-2,000 depending on bank (lower bound EUR 500, about USD 585 at USD 1.17/EUR); opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport (with court-interpreter translation where needed), stated purpose of account; sometimes proof of address.
min_deposit_fees: No minimum deposit generally; monthly maintenance around EUR 2-10; card issuance fee.
banks: Banca Intesa Beograd, Raiffeisen Banka, AIK Banka, OTP Banka Srbija, Unicredit Serbia.
restrictions: No remote opening for non-residents; non-residents can hold dinar and FX accounts; CRS reporting; scrutiny of Russia-linked flows.
alternatives: Authorised representative with power of attorney; Wise, Revolut.
cost_note: Banca Intesa Beograd's individuals' tariff (May 2024) lists RSD 220 per month for a non-resident dinar payment account (about USD 2.20 at RSD 100/USD) with no minimum deposit; a separate opening fee is not published and card issuance is charged extra.

documents: Passport, Greek tax number (AFM, obtainable via tax representative), proof of foreign address, proof of income or employment; translations may be needed.
min_deposit_fees: Low or no minimum deposit; monthly fees typically a few euros; non-resident specifics not published.
banks: Piraeus Bank (online with video identification, eligibility to be checked), National Bank of Greece, Eurobank, Alpha Bank (usually branch visit).
restrictions: AFM practically required, CRS reporting, signature may require one in-branch visit; legacy 2015 capital controls now lifted.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut or other EU neobanks for EUR IBAN.
cost_note: Greek banks (Piraeus, NBG, Eurobank, Alpha) quote low or no minimums and monthly fees of a few euros for residents, but non-resident figures are not published.

documents: Passport, CPR number (usually required) or foreign TIN at some banks, Danish address, reason for account.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Nordea (reportedly accepts foreign TIN in place of CPR), Sydbank (case-by-case); Danske Bank generally requires CPR.
restrictions: Post-Danske Bank scandal AML tightening, strong de-risking of non-residents, MobilePay requires CPR and Danish number.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, Payset or other EMIs offering Danish/EU IBANs.
cost_note: Non-residents generally cannot open personal accounts without a CPR number, so no applicable costs.

documents: Passport, proof of address (utility bill or tenancy contract), often Jordanian residence permit and personal number; source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: Ahli Bank current account minimum balance JOD 200; others not published.
banks: Housing Bank (HBTF) accepts passports from non-resident non-Jordanians for savings accounts; Ahli Bank and Jordan Islamic Bank require residency.
restrictions: CBJ AML/KYC rules, most banks require residency for current accounts, no remote opening for foreigners.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; local e-wallets require Jordanian ID or residency.
cost_note: Housing Bank (the bank accepting non-resident passports) does not publish non-resident savings costs; Ahli Bank's JOD 200 current-account minimum (about USD 282 at JOD 0.709/USD) applies only to residents.

documents: Passport or national ID, proof of foreign address, bank reference/statements from home country, economic reason for account, source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: National Bank of Bahrain, Bank ABC (non-resident acceptance case-by-case; most retail banks expect a CPR).
restrictions: CBB rulebook requires enhanced due diligence and documented acceptance criteria for non-residents; remote e-KYC only for Bahrainis.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; GCC private banking for high-net-worth clients.
cost_note: National Bank of Bahrain and Bank ABC do not publish non-resident personal account fees or minimums.

documents: Passport, proof of local address, photos, often residence permit; foreign-exchange account needed for transfers.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Attijari Bank Mauritanie, BMCI, Banque Nationale de Mauritanie (non-resident requirements not published).
restrictions: Foreign-exchange regulation by Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, limited correspondent access, cash-based economy.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut abroad; local mobile wallets (Bankily, Masrvi) need local SIM and ID.
cost_note: Attijari Bank Mauritanie, BMCI and BNM do not publish non-resident personal account fees or minimums.

documents: Passport (certified), proof of foreign address, bank reference or statements, source-of-funds evidence, occupation details.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; non-resident and private-banking accounts often expect a meaningful USD/EUR/GBP balance.
banks: MCB, SBM Bank, Absa Mauritius, AfrAsia Bank (non-resident accounts; some accept courier or introducer applications).
restrictions: Strict KYC after FATF grey-list exit, CRS reporting; foreign-currency accounts widely available, no exchange controls.
alternatives: Introduction via licensed management company; Wise, Revolut.
cost_note: An unofficial reproduction of MCB's non-resident terms cites a USD 3,000 minimum balance to open and a USD 100 annual maintenance fee (about USD 8.30/month) plus a USD 10 penalty below minimum; the opening fee is not published and figures are unconfirmed by an official tariff.

documents: Passport, residence permit (CERPAC), proof of Nigerian address, BVN enrolment, reference letters, passport photos.
min_deposit_fees: Low minimums for savings and domiciliary accounts; non-resident fees not published.
banks: Access Bank, GTBank, Zenith Bank open accounts for resident expatriates; 2025 non-resident BVN platform is for diaspora Nigerians only.
restrictions: Mandatory BVN, CBN FX restrictions and naira volatility, domiciliary account withdrawal limits.
alternatives: Brokers' foreign-investor accounts; Wise for NGN payments; fintechs (Opay, Moniepoint) need BVN/NIN.
cost_note: Foreign non-residents cannot open personal accounts (the 2025 non-resident BVN platform is for diaspora Nigerians only), so no applicable costs.

documents: Passport, proof of address, often residence proof, notarised or certified ID for non-resident applications; initial deposit.
min_deposit_fees: Monthly maintenance roughly XOF 1,000-6,000; opening deposit varies by bank, not published.
banks: Ecobank Senegal (possible non-resident opening with certified documents), CBAO Attijariwafa, Societe Generale Senegal, Bank of Africa Senegal.
restrictions: BCEAO/UEMOA foreign-exchange regulation of non-resident accounts, XOF pegged to EUR, branch visit usually needed.
alternatives: Wave and Orange Money mobile wallets (need local SIM/ID); Wise, Revolut.
cost_note: Monthly maintenance at Senegalese banks is roughly XOF 1,000-6,000 (lower bound about USD 1.80 at XOF 560/USD); opening fees and deposits at Ecobank Senegal are not published.

documents: Passport, proof of address, likely US SSN/ITIN or foreign TIN and local presence; requirements not published.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: BankPacific and Bank of Guam (US-chartered banks with Palau offices); non-resident acceptance unconfirmed.
restrictions: USD economy served by US banks subject to FATCA and US KYC rules; small local banking market.
alternatives: Keep funds in an Australian bank or Wise; Palau digital residency ID does not confer bank access.
cost_note: BankPacific and Bank of Guam do not publish non-resident fees or minimums, and acceptance is unconfirmed.
